chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. Why does the aim of love require both sound teaching and a good conscience?
chapters.1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his true child in faith. Timothy is to stay in Ephesus and stop certain people from teaching different doctrine. They occupy themselves with myths and endless lists of ancestors. The law is good when used lawfully, against the lawless. Paul thanks Christ, who put him in service though he was a persecutor. Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul calls himself the chief. Timothy is to fight the good fight with faith and a good conscience. Hymenaeus and Alexander have wrecked their faith.
chapters.2.lds: How does the claim about one mediator support prayer for everyone?
chapters.2.summary: Paul urges prayer for all people, and for kings and all in authority. The aim is a quiet and peaceful life. God wants all people to be saved and to know the truth. There is one God and one mediator, who gave himself for all. Men are to pray without anger. Women are to dress modestly and adorn themselves with good works. The letter says a woman should learn quietly and not teach a man. It gives Adam and Eve as its reason.
chapters.3.lds: Why does care for a household supply a test for care of the assembly?
chapters.3.summary: The letter gives the qualities of an overseer. He must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, and able to teach. He must not be a drinker, violent, or a lover of money. He must rule his own house well and not be a new convert. Servants of the assembly must also be tested first. Their wives must be reverent and faithful. Paul writes so Timothy will know how to behave in God’s house. The chapter ends with a short confession about Christ revealed in the flesh.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches becoming a faithful example despite youth. Why must Timothy's visible conduct support the instruction he gives?
chapters.4.summary: The Spirit says that in later times some will leave the faith. They will forbid marriage and command people to abstain from foods. The letter answers that God created foods to be received with thanks. Everything God made is good. Timothy is to teach this and avoid profane fables. Bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value for all things. No one should despise his youth. He is to attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching, and use his gift.
chapters.5.lds: How do family duties and tested testimony limit careless decisions about support?
chapters.5.summary: Timothy is to treat older men as fathers and older women as mothers. The assembly should honor widows who are truly alone. A widow with children or grandchildren should be cared for by them. A widow is enrolled only if she is sixty and known for good works. Younger widows should marry. Elders who rule well deserve double honor, for the worker deserves his wages. An accusation against an elder needs two or three witnesses. Timothy is told to use a little wine for his stomach.
chapters.6.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sound doctrine as protection against false instruction. How does generous sharing answer the temptation to treat faith as private gain?
chapters.6.summary: Servants are told to honor their masters so that God’s name is not blasphemed. The letter warns against teachers who think godliness is a way to gain. Godliness with contentment is great gain. We brought nothing into the world and can carry nothing out. The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Timothy is to flee these things and fight the good fight of faith. The rich are told not to be proud or to trust in uncertain riches. Timothy is to guard what was entrusted to him.
